title: Reduction of symmetric-power lifting for reductive groups to split simply connected DVR groups
statement: For a commutative ring $A$ and a flat affine finitely presented $A$-group scheme $H$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], use group-object diagrams over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ has the coordinate Hopf algebra maps; fixed vectors satisfy $\rho(m)=m\otimes1$. Equivariance means commutation with coactions. Tensor and dual modules have diagonal and contragredient coactions. Write $\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M$ for the degree-$n$ part of the commutative algebra freely generated by $M$, with the induced coaction. Let $P(A,H)$ denote the following property: For every rational $H$-module $M$, with no finiteness or flatness assumption, and every equivariant surjective $A$-linear map $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$ to the trivial module, there exist $n\geq1$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}^n_A M)^H$ such that $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q)=1$, under $\operatorname{Sym}^n_A A\simeq A$. Assume $P(A,H)$ holds whenever $A$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with algebraically closed residue field and $H$ is split semisimple simply connected. Here semisimple means that $H$ is smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and all its geometric fibres are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup; simply connected means that every central isogeny onto a geometric fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism. A central isogeny is a surjective homomorphism with finite central kernel, and solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial. Split means that $H$ has a split maximal torus and a Borel subgroup scheme containing it; these have fibrewise maximal-torus and maximal smooth connected solvable subgroups, and the torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$. Then $P(R,G)$ holds for every commutative ring $R$ and every smooth affine finitely presented $R$-group scheme $G$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] whose geometric fibres are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means that every geometric point is a unipotent matrix in a faithful representation, that is, $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, reductive-to-geometrically-reductive direction, reductions preceding the final determinant argument, printed p.527; use Lemma 9.2.5(2),(5), Proposition 9.3.1 (base change and descent), Proposition 9.5.1 (quotients and extensions). The result is the conditional reduction, not the geometric reductivity theorem itself; no SGA source is invoked. Local PDF WANTED; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf

proof.text: If $R=0$, every $R$-module is zero and $n=1$, $q=0$ maps to $1=0$. Assume $R\ne0$. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-etale-integral-models] to obtain a finite jointly surjective affine etale cover with $G_{B_i}\simeq(H_i)_{B_i}$ for split reductive integral models $H_i$. By clauses (1) and (4) of [lem-sfb-invariant-power-base-change-descent], it suffices to prove $P(\mathbf Z,H)$ for every split reductive $\mathbf Z$-group $H$: clause (1) then gives $P(B_i,(H_i)_{B_i})$, and clause (4) gives $P(R,G)$. An isomorphism of group schemes identifies coactions, invariant elements, and the same map $\lambda$, so the property is unchanged by the displayed isomorphisms.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, first two reductions in the reductive direction, p.527; corrected base-change/descent references are Proposition 9.3.1(i),(ii).

proof.text: For any ring $A$ and split torus $T=\mathbf G_m^r=D_A(\mathbf Z^r)$, prove $P(A,T)$ with $n=1$. Given $\lambda:M\twoheadrightarrow A$, choose $m$ with $\lambda(m)=1$. Apply [lem-sfb-group-algebra-coaction-grading] to the induced coaction on $\operatorname{Sym}_A M$. Its coefficient decomposition applied to $\iota(m)$ stays in degree one: the original coaction of $m$ lies in $M\otimes_A A[\mathbf Z^r]$, so its coefficients lie in $\iota(M)=\operatorname{Sym}^1_A M$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Write $\iota(m)=\sum_\chi a_\chi$. Equivariance of $\operatorname{Sym}(\lambda)$ and independence of the basis $e_\chi$ imply $\operatorname{Sym}(\lambda)(a_\chi)=0$ for $\chi\ne0$, since the target has trivial coaction. Thus $a_0$ is invariant and maps to $1$ in degree one. This calculation also covers $r=0$ and arbitrary torsion modules.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, p.527: the torus radical is geometrically reductive. Expanded directly by coefficient grading, Stacks 0EKK (lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm).

proof.text: Fix a split reductive $H$ over $\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-integral-radical-cover] and choose its two integral exact sequences $1\to T\to H\to Q\to1$ and $1\to F\to S\to Q\to1$. Here $T$ is a split torus, $Q$ is split semisimple, and $S$ is split semisimple simply connected. The same node states that their base changes stay exact and keep these properties. In particular, over any ring $A$, $T_A,H_A,Q_A,S_A$ and $F_A$ are flat affine finitely presented groups, and $F_A$ is finite locally free. Hence these sequences meet all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-invariant-power-exact-sequences], even in a residue characteristic where $F_A$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.3 and Exercise 6.5.2(i); the two structural reductions used in Alper Theorem 9.7.5, p.527.

proof.text: For each rational prime $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr] gives the Noetherian DVR $A_p=\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, with residue field $\mathbf F_p$. By [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], choose an algebraic closure $K_p$ of $\mathbf F_p$. It is a separable closure: Frobenius on the finite field is injective, hence surjective; an irreducible inseparable polynomial would have zero derivative and thus be a $p$th power, contradicting irreducibility. Let $C_p=A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to $K_p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] its residue field is $K_p$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3) identifies this colimit, with its $A_p$-algebra structure, with the strict local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}A_p$ at $\operatorname{Spec}K_p$. Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] to this scheme and geometric point: its original local ring is the Noetherian DVR $A_p$, so $C_p$ is a DVR. Finally [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] gives faithful flatness of $A_p\to C_p$. Thus these are DVRs with algebraically closed residue fields, rather than DVRs with merely separably closed imperfect residue fields.

source.place: Tags 0AP3 (lemma-henselization-dvr), 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization); algebra.tex Tag 04GP (lemma-strict-henselization). This makes Alper Theorem 9.7.5 DVR reduction explicit.

proof.text: By the assumed DVR case, $P(C_p,S_{C_p})$ holds: step 3 supplies split semisimplicity and simple connectedness and step 4 supplies the required base and residue field. The quotient clause of [lem-sfb-invariant-power-exact-sequences] applied to $S_{C_p}\to Q_{C_p}$ gives $P(C_p,Q_{C_p})$. Step 2 gives $P(C_p,T_{C_p})$. Apply the extension clause of that same node to $1\to T_{C_p}\to H_{C_p}\to Q_{C_p}\to1$, obtaining $P(C_p,H_{C_p})$. Neither application assumes that the module in the lifting problem is finite or free.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5, p.527: quotient and extension reductions; Proposition 9.5.1(i),(ii) in the formulation of Lemma 9.2.5(5).

proof.text: Clause (2) of [lem-sfb-invariant-power-base-change-descent] descends $P(C_p,H_{C_p})$ along the faithfully flat map $A_p\to C_p$ to $P(A_p,H_{A_p})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr], all maximal ideals of $\mathbf Z$ are $(p)$ for rational primes $p$. Clause (3) of the base-change/descent node therefore gives $P(\mathbf Z,H)$. This holds for every split reductive integral model $H$, which is exactly the sufficient assertion in step 1. It follows that $P(R,G)$ holds, with all modules allowed in the statement.

This is a first split of a node Q135 created on 2026-10-24, not a re-split; the parent lem-sfb-reductive-ring-invariant-power-lifting uses it only as the reduction premise. Alper and Conrad are not in local literature (WANTED), so I checked each new statement mathematically myself instead of against the cited pages. invariant-power-base-change-descent: (1) holds by the fibre product M x_B A, which is a subcomodule because A[H] is flat; (2) by invariants commuting with flat base change, so I_n B = B gives I_n = A; (3) by clearing denominators, raising to a common degree and taking a unit combination; (4) follows from (2). invariant-power-exact-sequences: the quotient clause holds because O(Q) -> O(S) is injective; the extension clause is Alper 9.5.1(2); nonreduced kernels such as mu_p are allowed. reductive-etale-integral-models: true over a nonzero ring; over Z a torus isomorphic to G_m^r gives free root spaces, so 'split' matches Conrad's. split-integral-radical-cover: true as the radical, the semisimple quotient and the simply connected cover with finite multiplicative kernel; tested on GL_n/PGL_n/SL_n with mu_n, on tori and on semisimple groups. Steps 1-6 checked against the cited statements: step 2 (torus, coefficient grading) really is elementary; step 4 goes Z_(p) -> strict henselization with residue field the algebraic closure of F_p (perfectness argument), then etale-local-ring-triples(3), strict-henselization-dvr and faithful flatness; steps 5-6 apply the hypothesis to S over C_p, then the quotient/extension clauses, then descent and the maximal-local clause.
